coverage.Required wording: Express a meaningful limitation of reference comparability AND why the comparison cannot establish disease effects or clinical diagnosis; for controls it cannot establish disease or overall normality. One statement may also support a case requirement.
coverage.Components: AND: comparability and inference limitations
coverage.rater1 reason: Sections 1 and 3 state unmatched reference, inseparable slow-speed/stroke effects and no disease/diagnosis inference.
coverage.rater2 reason: Sec.1: "not matched to this participant on age or speed ... no speed-matched healthy reference exists ... do not by themselves establish a disease effect, a severity grade, a mechanism, or a clinical diagnosis."
coverage.rater3 reason: Reference-comparability limit (pooled/unmatched/speed) and no-disease/no-normality inference limit both stated (Secs 1-3).

coverage.Required wording: Describe walking speed 0.21 m/s and that it is below the stated 0.80 m/s reference floor; no reference at this speed is supplied.
coverage.Components: AND: displayed speed and that it lies below the 0.80 m/s reference floor, so no speed-supported healthy reference exists in this dataset. Optional: cadence, speed-band label (not a functional claim). One sentence may also serve the comparability half of G03.
coverage.rater1 reason: Section 1 gives 0.21 m/s below 0.80 m/s and no speed-matched reference.
coverage.rater2 reason: Sec.1: "At 0.21 m/s this participant is far below that floor, so no speed-matched healthy reference exists in this dataset."
coverage.rater3 reason: Speed 0.21 m/s stated (Sec 1); below-floor/no-matched-reference meaning in reference paragraph.

coverage.Required wording: Identify the knee as the leading GVS difference AND another lower-limb difference using hip OR ankle. Exact GVS values are optional; identify the findings as reference-relative sagittal summary differences.
coverage.Components: AND: knee as leading AND (hip OR ankle). Stating which joint is larger is optional; asserting the reverse order is an error. Exact GVS values are optional; no waveform direction, phase or restriction is required.
coverage.rater1 reason: Rechecked Sections 3 and 4 against D01/D02 and the actual AND/OR components. Section 3 identifies knee largest followed by hip and ankle as sagittal reference differences.
coverage.rater2 reason: Re-read under D01/D02: the required joint(s) or route are identified by an explicit statement or an equivalent sentence elsewhere in the report (see original evidence), not by a value list alone. Covered stands.
coverage.rater3 reason: Required joint differences and rank conveyed (Sec 3 values + prominence statement/mention).

coverage.Required wording: Describe GAS envelope above its phase-specific reference mean at approximately 81% of the analysis cycle (displayed max |z| 21.7). Within each route, muscle identity AND mean-relative direction AND approximate cycle location are required. Exact max-|z| repetition is optional.
coverage.Components: Required for each route: muscle identity AND direction relative to the phase-specific reference mean AND approximate cycle location. Optional: exact max |z| value, comparison with the supplied endpoint span (descriptive only). Prohibited: percentile classification, gait phase, physiological onset, severity.
coverage.rater1 reason: Section 2 GAS gives above-mean direction at 81%, max |z| 21.7.
coverage.rater2 reason: Sec.2: "GAS (21.7, above reference at 81% of cycle)".
coverage.rater3 reason: Required muscle-direction-location conveyed via EMG table + direction statement (Sec 2).

coverage.Required wording: Describe EITHER ST envelope above its phase-specific reference mean at approximately 46% of the analysis cycle (displayed max |z| 6.4) OR VL envelope above its phase-specific reference mean at approximately 51% of the analysis cycle (displayed max |z| 6.4). One complete muscle-specific route is sufficient. Within each route, muscle identity AND mean-relative direction AND approximate cycle location are required. Exact max-|z| repetition is optional.
coverage.Components: OR: one complete route suffices. Required for each route: muscle identity AND direction relative to the phase-specific reference mean AND approximate cycle location. Optional: exact max |z| value, comparison with the supplied endpoint span (descriptive only). Prohibited: percentile classification, gait phase, physiological onset, severity.
coverage.rater1 reason: Section 2 ST above mean at 46% and VL above mean at 51% each complete an allowed route.
coverage.rater2 reason: Sec.2 table "ST ... 6.4, above reference, at 46%" and "VL ... 6.4, above reference, at 51%".
coverage.rater3 reason: Required muscle-direction-location conveyed via EMG table + direction statement (Sec 2).

coverage.Required wording: Describe the supplied successive-footfall step-length index -62.4% and its meaning: the paretic step is shorter.
coverage.Components: AND: displayed index and the direction supported by its sign. Optional: formula, definition wording. Acceptable phrasing for small displayed values: "a small difference with the paretic step slightly shorter/longer" (not a cutoff). Prohibited: restating the index as a percentage shortening (E01), severity grades, whole-gait symmetry generalization (E07 issue, not an omission).
coverage.rater1 reason: Section 1 gives -62.4%, successive-footfall definition and shorter paretic step.
coverage.rater2 reason: Sec.1: "-62.4% ... the paretic step is the shorter one".
coverage.rater3 reason: Index -62.4% stated with paretic-shorter meaning (Sec 1).

coverage.rater3 reason: Reference-comparability limit (pooled/unmatched/speed) and no-disease/no-normality inference limit both stated (Secs 1-3).

coverage.rater3 reason: v2 correction: ankle explicitly largest single GVS (18.23), followed by hip (15.64)/knee (15.32, Sec 3 line 67). v1 table-only rationale was factually wrong.

coverage.Required wording: Describe GAS envelope above its phase-specific reference mean at approximately 57% of the analysis cycle (displayed max |z| 10.1). coverage.Required wording: Describe the ERS envelope above its phase-specific reference mean at approximately 80% of the analysis cycle.

coverage.rater2 reason: Sec.2: "ERS (5.8 at 80%)" with table "above @ 80%".
coverage.rater3 reason: Required muscle-direction-location conveyed via EMG table + direction statement (Sec 2).

coverage.Required wording: Describe the supplied successive-footfall step-length index 5.7% and its meaning: the paretic step is longer.
coverage.Components: AND: displayed index and the direction supported by its sign. Optional: formula, definition wording. Acceptable phrasing for small displayed values: "a small difference with the paretic step slightly shorter/longer" (not a cutoff). Prohibited: restating the index as a percentage shortening (E01), severity grades, whole-gait symmetry generalization (E07 issue, not an omission).
coverage.rater1 reason: Section 1 gives +5.7%, successive-footfall definition and longer paretic step.
coverage.rater2 reason: Sec.1: "+5.7% ... the paretic step is the longer of the two".
coverage.rater3 reason: Index 5.7% stated with paretic-longer meaning (Sec 1).

coverage.Required wording: Express a meaningful limitation of reference comparability AND why the comparison cannot establish disease effects or clinical diagnosis; for controls it cannot establish disease or overall normality. One statement may also support a case requirement.
coverage.Components: AND: comparability and inference limitations
coverage.rater1 reason: Section 3 explicitly states limited matching despite in-range speed and inability to isolate a stroke effect or establish diagnosis.
coverage.rater2 reason: Sec.3: "The pooled reference and calibration distributions have limited comparability to this participant; the EMG, CCI, and kinematic comparisons cannot isolate a stroke-specific disease effect or establish a clinical diagnosis".
coverage.rater3 reason: Reference-comparability limit (pooled/unmatched/speed) and no-disease/no-normality inference limit both stated (Secs 1-3).

coverage.Required wording: Describe walking speed 1.36 m/s and that it is within the stated reference speed range; this does not establish individual matching.
coverage.Components: AND: displayed speed and that it lies within the supplied 0.80-1.79 m/s span AND that an in-range speed does not establish an individually matched reference. Optional: position within the span. One sentence may also serve the comparability half of G03.
coverage.rater1 reason: Sections 1 and 3 give 1.36 m/s within 0.80-1.79 m/s and explicitly state that this does not establish an appropriately matched comparison.
coverage.rater2 reason: Sec.1 speed 1.36 m/s; Sec.3: "Although 1.36 m/s lies within the cohort's overall 0.80-1.79 m/s speed range, this does not establish an appropriately matched comparison".
coverage.rater3 reason: Speed 1.36 m/s stated (Sec 1); in-range-but-unmatched meaning stated (reference paragraph).

coverage.Required wording: Identify knee AND pelvis as the principal GVS differences AND distinguish the pelvic GVS difference from its small measured excursion (pelvic ROM 2.1 degrees). Exact GVS values are optional; identify the findings as reference-relative sagittal summary differences.
coverage.Components: AND: knee AND pelvis AND contrast between pelvic GVS and small pelvic excursion (ROM 2.1). No offset direction, restriction or normative claim. Exact values optional.
coverage.rater1 reason: Rechecked Sections 3 and 4 against D01/D02 and the actual AND/OR components. Section 3 identifies knee and pelvis as the largest GVS differences and lists pelvic ROM 2.1 degrees, but does not distinguish the pelvic GVS difference from the small measured excursion as required.
coverage.rater2 reason: D02: knee and pelvis are identified, but the required contrast between the large pelvic GVS and the small pelvic excursion (ROM 2.1, table only) is never conveyed. Partially covered stands.
coverage.rater3 reason: v2 correction: knee/pelvis prominence stated (line 44) but required contrast between pelvic GVS and small ROM (2.1) is absent; table value alone does not draw it.

coverage.Required wording: Describe EITHER (A) the ST envelope above its phase-specific reference mean at approximately 37% of the analysis cycle OR (B) broad ST mean-envelope above-threshold extent spanning the cycle boundary. One complete route suffices. The displayed max |z| 4.6 and coverage 79% are optional anchors.
coverage.Components: Route A: ST AND above-mean direction AND approximate location. Route B: ST AND broad detected above-threshold extent AND boundary spanning. Exact magnitude, coverage and segment endpoints are optional. A displayed 4.6-versus-4.61 comparison is permitted; it does not determine hidden unrounded classification or physiological normality. No separate uncertainty sentence is a coverage component.
coverage.rater1 reason: Section 2 ST gives above-reference mean direction at 37%, completing route A; its 79% boundary-spanning coverage also supports route B.
coverage.rater2 reason: Route A: Sec.2 table "ST | 50%-64%; 79%-42% (wrap) | 79% | 0.84 | 4.6; above, at 37%". Route B also present (wrapping interval, 79% coverage, boundary continuity named).
coverage.rater3 reason: Required muscle-direction-location conveyed via EMG table + direction statement (Sec 2).

coverage.Required wording: Describe the supplied successive-footfall step-length index -5.1% and its meaning: the paretic step is shorter.
coverage.Components: AND: displayed index and the direction supported by its sign. Optional: formula, definition wording. Acceptable phrasing for small displayed values: "a small difference with the paretic step slightly shorter/longer" (not a cutoff). Prohibited: restating the index as a percentage shortening (E01), severity grades, whole-gait symmetry generalization (E07 issue, not an omission).
coverage.rater1 reason: Section 1 gives -5.1%, successive-footfall definition and shorter paretic step.
coverage.rater2 reason: Sec.1: "-5.1%, using the successive-footfall definition, indicating a shorter paretic-side step".
coverage.rater3 reason: Index -5.1% stated with paretic-shorter meaning (Sec 1).

coverage.Required wording: Identify the participant as a healthy control AND state that the leave-one-out comparison excludes this participant. IF speed is discussed, state it was not supplied; IF cadence is discussed, state it was not supplied; IF the task-specific paretic/non-paretic step-length index is discussed, state it is not applicable. Each branch is triggered only by that domain. Exact reference count 137 is optional.
coverage.Components: AND: healthy-control provenance AND self-exclusion from the leave-one-out reference. Conditional, per domain: speed not supplied; cadence not supplied; task-specific paretic/non-paretic index not applicable. Optional: count 137. G03 applies separately once. A correct core with one missing AND component is partial.
coverage.rater1 reason: Sections 1 and 3 provide control membership and exclusion of Sub07; discussed speed/cadence are unavailable and task-specific symmetry index not applicable.
coverage.rater2 reason: Sec.1: "control group"; Sec.3: "137 healthy participants, excluding Sub07"; "Gait speed and cadence are not provided"; paretic/non-paretic index "not applicable".
coverage.rater3 reason: Control provenance + leave-one-out self-exclusion stated; discussed domains (speed/cadence/paretic index) correctly marked not-supplied/not-applicable.

coverage.rater3 reason: Reference-comparability limit (pooled/unmatched/speed) and no-disease/no-normality inference limit both stated (Secs 1-3).

coverage.Required wording: Convey EITHER (A) GPS-like 2.55 as a composite sagittal difference from the reference OR (B) knee AND ankle as relatively larger joint-curve differences OR (C) that the four supplied sagittal GVS values span approximately 1.44-3.13 degrees. One complete route suffices.

Route C: the four-channel GVS scope AND approximate lower/upper values; a normative smallness label and a list of every joint value are not required. No route establishes normal gait.

coverage.rater1 reason: Revise the provisional Partially covered/Pending judgment to Covered/Final after integrating the report. Sections 1 and 3 identify unmatched pooled comparison and explain that differences may reflect speed, demographic and calibration effects rather than isolated physiology. Section 4 explicitly says speed matching cannot be determined. The CCI paragraph says empirical-range membership does not independently establish normal muscle function; the ROM note says the measurement does not define clinical restriction; the max-|z| paragraph denies a clinical severity interpretation. rater1.Original locations: Section 2, report line 52 (ERS location claim only)

rater2.Exact quote: the mean envelope below threshold between the retained interval endpoints at 34% and 44%
rater2.Reason: Error, category E03 (threshold/detection-rule overinterpretation), low consequence. Model input: ERS retained interval 44%-34% (wraps the cycle boundary), 90% of cycle above threshold, minimum retained interval 3% of the cycle; the retained span (44%-100% plus 0%-34%) equals 90%. Read in context, the sentence first states correctly that each coverage below 100% leaves a remainder of the cycle not counted as above threshold, then gives the example "the mean envelope below threshold between the retained interval endpoints at 34% and 44%", i.e. it asserts that the mean envelope is below threshold throughout the 10% gap. What the input establishes: the retained run ended at 34% and resumed at 44%, so at least some samples in between did not exceed threshold; and the displayed coverage (90%) matches the retained span, so any above-threshold excursion inside the gap is short (within whole-percent rounding of the endpoints and coverage, at most about 1-1.5% of the cycle). What it does not establish: that every sample between 34% and 44% is below threshold. The rubric (section 8) states that the 3% minimum-duration rule filters short above-threshold runs, not below-threshold gaps, so a non-retained region cannot be equated with a strictly below-threshold region; equality-to-threshold and masked samples also fall in the complement (R03). The wording therefore makes a plausible but not supported statement about the envelope throughout the region. Same reading as applied to "the mean envelope was below threshold outside those intervals" (R0C44EC0AE866FB58, rater2 I003, Error E03). The same sentence's later caution about rounded coverage concerns the opposite direction (no-gap claims) and does not qualify this example. This assessment is separate from the report's normalization question (line 100), which rater2 does not record as an error. No control flag is involved (stroke report).
rater2.Disposition basis: Explicit human residual response; no new global rule adopted.

rater3.Exact quote: the mean envelope below threshold between the retained interval endpoints at 34% and 44%
rater3.Reason: Revised from Pending to Error E03 under the strict rule adopted on 2026-09-20: any status assertion about a gap (non-retained) region that goes beyond the retained-interval output is Error, regardless of hedging. Numbers verified and unchanged: ERS retained interval 44%-34% wrapping with 90% coverage (input line 35), complement 34%-44%; all seven muscles below 100% coverage. The defect is the asserted region status itself: "the mean envelope below threshold between the retained interval endpoints at 34% and 44%" conflates not-retained with below-threshold. Under the supplied detector rule (above-threshold runs retained only if >=3% of cycle, input line 7), a sub-duration above-threshold burst inside 34%-44% would leave no retained interval, so the complement's strict below-threshold status is a detection result the input does not contain (same family as A003; equality/masking add the R03 caveat). The in-sentence coverage cautions limit the claim's scope but do not retract the asserted gap-region status, so they do not save it under the strict rule. Separate from the normalization question.
rater3.Disposition basis: Explicit human residual response; no new global rule adopted.
